5-6: The perimeter of a figure of cells, given by a drawing or by the names of its cells: the sides on the outside.
The area left when the corners of a square of cells are taken away.
Cells that share a whole side with a given group of cells: how many there are.
A figure of cells: its area in square units, from the side of one cell.
Dominoes on a small board: how many ways to place one.
A few square tiles joined side to side: the largest or the smallest perimeter the shape can have.
A bar of squares broken along its lines: the pieces and the breaks.
Two rectangles of cells that overlap: the area they cover together.
The largest square of cells that fits in a figure.
A figure of cells cut into equal parts along the lines of its cells.
A figure of cells with no axis of symmetry, and one cell added to it: how many axes of symmetry the new figure can have.
Small rectangles cut from a big one: the area gives the most there could be, and laying some one way and some the other shows whether that many fit.
Strips of 1, 2, 3 and so on laid into one rectangle, both sides longer than 1: strips paired to the same length make equal rows, the longest alone a row when the count is odd.
A square sawn into pieces of two shapes with a known total length of the cuts: how many of each, from the pieces' areas and their perimeters.
A rectangle drawn on a grid and the figure joining the midpoints of its sides: that figure has half the rectangle's area.
A straight line across a board of cells, or the diagonal of a rectangle of cells: each grid line it crosses starts a new cell, less the corners it passes through.

5-6.idea: A goat tied in a cell beside a shed drawn on squared paper, the rope's length in steps written in that cell: how many cells it reaches round the shed.
A shape of cells with a piece drawn in it: how many such pieces, turned but never turned over, cover the shape, or that they cannot.
Cuts drawn along the lines of a figure of cells: the pieces it falls into, cells joined by a side that is not cut staying together.
A figure of cells and a dashed axis through the middle of its frame: the fewest cells to fill so that the figure is the same on both sides of the axis.
